frameworks.name: Agentic mailbox retrieval loop
frameworks.definition: A reusable method for turning an email archive into a system that can retrieve, reason over, and act on messages through explicit tool use.
steps: Ingest mailbox messages incrementally.
Normalize and chunk email content while preserving thread metadata.
Index content with searchable metadata and retrieval support.
Expose retrieval as a tool the agent can call.
Use an LLM planner to decide whether to search, answer, draft, or act.
Ground outputs in retrieved snippets before any action.
frameworks.when_to_use: When you want an assistant to work across a large Outlook mailbox, not just answer questions from a fixed document set.
failure_modes: The agent answers from memory instead of retrieval, producing hallucinations.
Thread context is lost during chunking, so responses miss the full conversation.
Tool access is too broad, causing unsafe or unintended actions.

playbooks.title: Build an AI assistant over Outlook email
playbooks.trigger: You want to search, summarize, draft replies from, and possibly act on a large Outlook mailbox.
steps: Define the main use cases: retrieval, summarization, drafting, triage, or action.
Ingest Outlook mail incrementally so new messages are captured without reprocessing everything.
Preserve thread structure, sender, date, and subject as retrieval metadata.
Index the mailbox so the assistant can search both by meaning and by keywords.
Wrap search as a tool and let the agent decide when to retrieve before answering.
Constrain the system prompt so outputs stay grounded in retrieved messages.
Add human approval for any outward action such as sending mail.
playbooks.applicable_when: Best for advisory, executive-assistant, or knowledge-management use cases where email is the primary corporate memory source.

claims.text: Agents combine retrieval, reasoning, and action.
Vector search combined with keyword search is presented as the easiest path for email retrieval in the described architecture.
claims.source_excerpt: Azure AI Search hybrid (vector + BM25) is the path of least resistance.

frameworks.name: Incremental RAG performance triage
frameworks.definition: A pragmatic method for improving an existing RAG system by sequencing the highest-impact, lowest-disruption changes before considering a redesign.
steps: Diagnose the main bottleneck across retrieval, generation, and serving.
Apply small, local optimizations that reduce latency or improve retrieval quality.
Measure impact after each change before adding the next one.
Only redesign the architecture if the bottleneck remains structural.
frameworks.when_to_use: When an existing RAG app works but feels slow, brittle, or hard to scale and you want fast wins without a rewrite.
failure_modes: Optimizing the wrong layer while the main bottleneck is elsewhere.
Making too many changes at once and losing attribution for improvements.
Jumping to a full rebuild before exhausting low-effort fixes.

frameworks.name: Clean-sheet RAG architecture selection
frameworks.definition: A decision framework for designing a new RAG system by separating ingestion, storage, retrieval, reranking, and serving into the simplest scalable arrangement.
steps: Define the expected scale, latency tolerance, and concurrency needs.
Choose durable storage for source data and a dedicated retrieval layer for vectors.
Add reranking if retrieval precision materially affects answer quality.
Separate ingestion jobs from user-facing inference paths.
Design the UI and API layers so they can scale independently.
frameworks.when_to_use: When starting a new RAG project or replacing a design that has outgrown its prototype architecture.
failure_modes: Overengineering the stack for a small workload.
Conflating prototype convenience with production readiness.
Choosing infrastructure that improves elegance but not the user experience.

playbooks.title: Sequence high-impact RAG changes for implementation
playbooks.trigger: You already have a working RAG app and want a prioritized list of tactical improvements to hand to a coding assistant.
steps: Start with cold-start and memory fixes that reduce latency immediately.
Add caching for repeated embeddings or repeated expensive calls.
Insert a reranking step after initial retrieval to improve answer quality.
Move heavy inference off the request thread so interfaces remain responsive.
Remove duplicate pipelines or obsolete paths that create maintenance drag.
Apply chunking and index compression if retrieval quality and scale still need improvement.
playbooks.applicable_when: The goal is to improve performance substantially without changing the overall product shape or introducing a full new platform.

frameworks.name: Marco de elegibilidad concesional para carreteras en España
frameworks.definition: Método para juzgar, a nivel estratégico, si una infraestructura vial puede estructurarse como concesión o PPP sin desvirtuar el reparto real de riesgos.
steps: Verificar encaje legal y contractual del activo en la normativa de concesiones aplicable.
Comprobar si existe transferencia efectiva de riesgo operacional al privado.
Analizar el tratamiento SEC-2010 y el impacto potencial en déficit y deuda.
Evaluar si la estructura financiera depende de garantías, mínimos de ingresos o apoyo público excesivo.
Contrastar viabilidad técnica, costes de inversión/explotación y valor por dinero para el contribuyente.
frameworks.when_to_use: Cuando se quiera hacer una primera criba estratégica de una carretera existente o futura antes de profundizar en modelización financiera o contractual.
failure_modes: Confundir alivio presupuestario con verdadera transferencia de riesgo.
Diseñar garantías públicas que vacían de contenido la concesión.
Omitir el impacto de la desindexación y de los costes de largo plazo.
Analizar solo la demanda sin integrar riesgos de construcción y disponibilidad.

claims.text: La Directiva 2014/23/UE exige transferencia efectiva del riesgo operacional para que exista un contrato de concesión.
claims.source_excerpt: la Directiva 2014/23/UE ... exige la transferencia efectiva del riesgo operacional al concesionario como rasgo definitorio

claims.text: Bajo SEC-2010, una concesión puede quedar fuera de balance solo si el privado asume la mayor parte de los riesgos de construcción y disponibilidad o demanda.
claims.source_excerpt: solo puede considerarse fuera del balance público ... si el socio privado asume la mayor parte de los riesgos de construcción y disponibilidad/demanda

claims.text: La Ley 2/2015 de Desindexación de la Economía Española prohíbe la indexación automática de contratos públicos a la inflación.
claims.source_excerpt: la Ley 2/2015 de Desindexación de la Economía Española, que prohíbe la indexación automática de contratos públicos a la inflación

claims.text: En SEC-2010, la deuda de una concesión no computa como pública salvo que la Administración financie la mayor parte, garantice más del 50% de la deuda o asegure ingresos o rentabilidad mínima.
claims.source_excerpt: la deuda de la concesión no computará como pública excepto si la Administración financia la mayor parte de la obra, garantiza más del 50% de la deuda del proyecto o asegura ... un ingreso o rentabilidad mínima

frameworks.name: High-margin part-time career pivot
frameworks.definition: A method for reshaping senior expertise into a smaller number of high-value engagements that preserve income while reducing weekly hours.
steps: Define a hard cap on working time and a target annual income.
Select services that are brief, premium, and expertise-led.
Reposition the personal brand around scarcity, seniority, and responsiveness.
Use repeatable channels such as expert networks, board recruiting, and direct warm contacts.
Productise knowledge into training, licensing, or other one-to-many offers.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a senior professional wants to earn more while working substantially fewer hours.
failure_modes: Chasing low-value work that fills the calendar but not the income target.
Offering too many services instead of a focused premium niche.
Underpricing senior expertise and weakening market positioning.
Allowing travel and admin to recreate a full-time workload.

playbooks.title: Pivot an experienced engineer into part-time high-income advisory work
playbooks.trigger: A senior technical professional wants to leave full-time employment for a lighter, more lucrative working pattern.
steps: Set explicit income and hours targets before choosing any service line.
Prioritise advisory formats with high fees and low delivery time, such as expert calls or second opinions.
Package existing expertise into a premium niche and update the public profile accordingly.
Activate warm networks and specialist intermediaries to generate recurring opportunities.
Use simple pricing tiers and clear contract terms to protect part-time boundaries.
playbooks.applicable_when: The person already has deep domain expertise, reputation, and client-facing credibility, and wants to monetise that through short engagements or fractional roles.

claims.text: Senior PPP experts in developed-market advisory or expert-network work can target around €2,300/day if aiming for roughly €250k/year over 96–120 billable days.
claims.source_excerpt: Set a revenue goal (e.g., €250k/year gross). Compute your required day-rate: €250k ÷ 110 days ≈ €2,300/day. That number is achievable for senior PPP experts in developed-market advisory or expert-network work

frameworks.name: ToR-to-Proposal Alignment Loop
frameworks.definition: A structured advisory method for turning a client's terms of reference into a tailored services proposal by aligning scope, structure, tone, and evidence to the buyer's requirements.
steps: Read the ToR for explicit deliverables, constraints, evaluation criteria, and submission format.
Extract the client's priorities and implied decision criteria.
Map each proposal section directly to the ToR requirements.
Draft the proposal in the client's language and sequence.
Review for gaps, misalignment, and unsupported claims.
Iterate until the proposal reads as a direct response to the ToR.
frameworks.when_to_use: When preparing a services proposal, bid, or response document from a client-issued terms of reference.
failure_modes: Writing a generic proposal that does not track the ToR closely.
Omitting mandatory sections or evaluation-relevant content.
Overemphasizing capabilities that are not requested by the client.

playbooks.title: Draft a Services Proposal from a Terms of Reference
playbooks.trigger: A client has issued a terms of reference and you need to produce a tailored proposal response.
steps: Identify the client’s objective, scope, constraints, and evaluation logic.
Create a proposal skeleton that mirrors the ToR structure.
Draft each section to answer the client's stated requirements directly.
Use concise, professional language and include only relevant experience.
Check that the final draft addresses all mandatory items before submission.
playbooks.applicable_when: Useful for consultants, advisors, and bid teams preparing formal service proposals for procurement or client selection processes.
